title: The Lord forgives whom he will, but his people must forgive all
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Kirtland, Ohio, on 11 September 1831. He was preparing to move to Hiram to resume his Bible revision. Some who went to Missouri that summer came back disappointed. Ezra Booth had turned against Joseph Smith, and on 6 September a conference barred Booth from preaching. Edward Partridge had also clashed with Joseph Smith in Missouri over the land being bought.
summary: The revelation tells the elders that the Lord has forgiven their sins this once. Joseph Smith keeps the keys of the mysteries while he obeys, though he too has sinned. The elders must forgive all men, while the Lord forgives whom he will. Ezra Booth and Isaac Morley are named for not keeping the law, and Morley is forgiven. Edward Partridge has sinned and will be forgiven if he repents. Kirtland is to remain a strong hold for five years, so Frederick G. Williams keeps his farm. The revelation calls today a day of sacrifice and tithing, and says great things come from small things. It ends by saying the Lord requires the heart and a willing mind, and that Zion will flourish.

contextNote.title: Leaving judgment to God
contextNote.text: Leaders had quarreled in Missouri, and Ezra Booth had turned against Joseph Smith. Verse 8 recalls disciples of old who would not forgive each other and were chastened. Verse 9 says the one who does not forgive carries “the greater sin” before the Lord. Verse 10 sets the rule: the Lord forgives whom he will, but they must forgive all. Verses 12–13 add that church discipline still applies to the unrepentant, without withholding forgiveness. In this passage, forgiving means leaving judgment to God, as verse 11 phrases it.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 64–66 takes its title from verse 34. Verse 11 offers words to say in your heart toward someone who wronged you; how do verses 9–10 explain why that matters?

newPeople.name: Ezra Booth
newPeople.why: named in v. 15; former Methodist minister and elder who went to Missouri in 1831, then turned against Joseph Smith

reviewNote: Read all 43 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 11 September 1831, as Joseph Smith prepared to move to Hiram and others prepared to go to Zion in October. JSP historical introduction gave Booth’s disillusionment, his 6 September censure, and the Partridge dispute. Booth’s prior Methodist ministry is from general history, not the JSP introduction read here.
